name: Oasis Gas Pipeline / Clint Export Project

values.Owner: Oasis Pipe Line Company Texas LP

researcher_notes: A natural gas trade news story from June 2009 says FERC approved a border-crossing authorization and presidential permit (docket CP09-47) for Oasis Pipeline LP and Oasis Pipe Line Company Texas LP. The same story describes the Clint Export Project: 188 miles of 36-inch pipe from the Waha Hub in West Texas to near Clint in El Paso County, about 600 MMcf/d, to deliver to Tarahumara Pipeline in Chihuahua. A Federal Register notice from February 2009 covers the same application. Both pages loaded and name Oasis and Clint. The story says the Texas portion needed Texas regulator approval. This is a different line from the existing Oasis Gas Pipeline row P0234, which is the operating 966 mile system, and it is not the Comanche Trail line. Meets the add threshold: named sponsor, endpoints, permit application and approval, and about 188 miles of new pipe. No source found showing construction, an in-service date, or a formal cancellation. Status cancelled is inferred from 17 years of no build and later projects taking this corridor, so ShelvedCancelledType is inferred and no cancelled ref is given. The 2009 story gives a cost of 3.6 million dollars, which looks wrong for this size of pipe, so no cost is staged. Both refs trace to the one 2009 FERC application, so independence is weak; tier medium. Parent/owner: Oasis Pipe Line Company Texas LP would own and Oasis would operate; Energy Transfer LP is the parent per the Tarahumara partner naming, which was not directly verified, so check before applying. Route: none found, no official map. ProposalYear is 2009 from the application date. Reviewer should decide whether to keep as cancelled or shelved.
